question: How does the Lord's reply reframe Arjuna's role in battle?
premises: The Lord names Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and other heroes
They are already slain by the Lord; Arjuna should fight without distress
The reply is summarized as the Lord's answer to Arjuna's earlier words
inference: Arjuna is instrument while the Lord has already accomplished the slaying
uncertainties: Long fused prose compounds are kept whole
plain_english: Slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and other world-heroes; they have been slain by me, so do not be distressed; fight, and you will conquer rivals in battle. This here is the Lord's reply concerning the world's knowing-and-unknowing self; it is said that from pure, impure, and mixed awareness there is devouring. You fed the secret summarized in this chapter; may it be for those capable of immediate awareness. How much labor of line-writing; may we rest in stability. Here what was said by me: when they are slain, you, glorious one, be instrument. Thus by the Lord that was replied to what was said earlier by Arjuna: we do not know this; which of us is greater, and so on.
